reviews.text:
Hello Christian Albor.

Thank you for sharing your opinion about our 24-hour veterinary service.
Best regards from the team.

We went in scared because we thought it was a tick 😱 and it was a wart 🤪🤣 Mercedes took care of us. She calmed us down and explained perfectly how to identify them!! Thank you for your empathy towards us and the attention and affection you showed our dog!! ❤️🙏 …

Hello Nacho Serrano.
Thank you very much for your feedback.
Best regards.

Hello Alejandro Fuentes Cantillana.

Thank you very much for your feedback about our veterinary hospital. We'd be delighted to see you again.

Best regards.

I took my sick kitten in; he needed to be admitted, and I was very scared and crying. Both the assistants and the veterinarian who saw him, Adriana, treated me with so much kindness and patience. I was especially impressed by Nines, the cleaning and maintenance woman at the clinic. From the moment she saw me, she was incredibly kind and attentive, and she did her job professionally. Many thanks to all the medical professionals for healing and caring for my kitten with such love.
Best dental cleaning my Pomeranian has ever gotten. Thank you Jaime!

I'm so grateful to the entire team at Medivet Delicias. My dog ​​had a tumor on his spleen that caused bleeding, and they had to operate to remove it. From the very first moment, the care and professionalism were excellent, and luckily, everything went well and the tumor turned out to be benign.

It's not a cheap place, but quality comes at a price, and when your pet's health is at stake, it's absolutely worth it. Thank you for taking such good care of my dog. 🐶❤️
Great job to this clinic for the care they gave our pet Bellota (a toy poodle). A top-notch clinic.
Professional, attentive and friendly service
Fantastic service, very respectful and professional.

The team that has cared for our cat Thomas has been very attentive. Both Patricia, who has been most involved in his care and has been wonderful with him, and Paloma, who looked after him over the weekend, have been fantastic. Thais came in with a very acute case of gastritis and a viral infection, and they advised us to have a gastroscopy and an esophageal tube inserted. It hasn't been an easy process, but they have been a great help to us, his guardians. We are so happy that Patricia has been caring for him all this time because she has been especially attentive, as has Paloma, who was very caring.
If I had to mention anything negative, it would be the reception staff, who were sometimes more or less friendly, depending on who was helping. Also, regarding phone calls, we had to be a bit persistent, although I understand that when you have a lot of work, it's difficult to get to everything.

I will never have enough words to thank them.

I found an abandoned cat, discovered she was very sick, and took her there.

She was in critical condition, with a creatinine level of 16, completely incompatible with life. Thanks to the professionals, their patience, and everything else, my kitten is now as healthy as can be.

They also call you several times a day to explain everything; they explain it all so well. You can tell they are people who truly care about the animals they treat. I truly owe them everything ❤️, especially the life of my Pepa (well, Paquito, who turned out to be a boy, haha).
They helped me with my dog ​​in a complicated case and they provide excellent and fast service!
Very nice people, both professionally and personally. Highly recommended if your pet needs veterinary care.

We want to express our deepest gratitude to the entire Medivet Delicias team for the care we received. In such a painful moment as saying goodbye to our beloved Asterix, we found not only great professionalism but also tremendous compassion.

I want to give a very special mention to Edrei Marrero, head of hospitalization. His empathy, his warmth, and the gentle way he supported us made such a difficult time much more bearable. I have no words to describe the care he gave us. He made us feel understood, supported, and comforted when we needed it most.

Edrei, thank you so much, my friend, from the bottom of my heart. People like you dignify this profession and leave an indelible mark on those of us fortunate enough to encounter them in such a difficult time.

Thank you also to the entire team for caring for Asterix with such respect and love until the very end. We will never forget your kindness.

I am very upset with the staff. I took my dog ​​there a week ago; he was already sick. They ran a lot of tests on him, making him suffer, giving us false hope, and taking our money—€4000. Finally, on Saturday, we had to have him put down.

I do not recommend leaving a loved one at this clinic. My kitten was hospitalized for almost two weeks, and in my experience, instead of improving, her condition worsened.

When she was discharged that afternoon, I noticed she was worse than ever: very lethargic, weak, and in a state that worried me greatly. That same night, I had to rush her to the Puchol Veterinary Clinic, where they tried everything possible to save her, but sadly, she passed away a few hours later.
Besides the enormous financial cost, the pain I'm left with is indescribable. What hurts the most is thinking that I trusted she would receive the best possible care, and the outcome was devastating.

This is my personal experience, and for that reason, I would not recommend this clinic to anyone who wants to leave their pet with the peace of mind that they will be in the best hands. I deeply regret having made that decision, and it's a feeling I still live with every day.

Excellent help at a critical time and very kind treatment.

2.8.2026
I have to change my review. The clinic has become just a money-making machine. My dog ​​is sick, we've seen a different doctor every time, blood tests have no results, and they have no idea how to help us! What's going on? We're going to change clinics to find someone with experience.

It will be a month in a few days since our beloved Nuskita passed away, leaving us devastated and immersed in a deep sadness that, to this day, is insurmountable. But I must thank all the veterinarians and receptionists who treated her, especially Claudia, Bárbara, and Edrei, who treated her and us with such kindness.

Thank you for everything. A big hug to you all.

My cat Bicho had a brain tumor that was detected in a CT scan. He was going to die, but they were finally able to operate. They saved his life, and two months after the operation, he has recovered all his functions, his fur, and his stubbornness. It's as if he never had a tumor; his recovery still amazes me.

The staff were always very kind and didn't hesitate to answer all our questions, of which there were many. They were patient and compassionate with our pain and uncertainty. They saved his life, and I am very grateful, especially to Mar, Silvia, and Cristina, and to the surgeon, Juanmi.
It's not a cheap clinic, that's true; it cost us an arm and a leg, but I can't complain when they saved my cat and treated him with so much love, despite him throwing terrible tantrums the entire time he was hospitalized.

TERRIBLE EXPERIENCE

I waited almost two months before writing this review so I wouldn't be speaking from the anger I felt when I left the MEDIVET DELICIAS clinic. I admitted my senior cat (15 years old) with severe vomiting, dehydration, and loss of appetite. He was hospitalized overnight. Of course, the costs of hospitalization, fluid therapy, ultrasound, pain medication, blood tests, etc., must be paid upfront, not at the end of the treatment. It's like putting your cat in a luxury hotel. Both the doctor who saw me in the emergency room and the veterinarian who gave me the results were professional and wonderful. I have no complaints about them. The tests came back clear, but the cat still wasn't eating. I decided to take him to my trusted veterinarian.

When they brought him back, they did so without any kind of protocol. They handed him over right there in reception, with other animals, dogs, people, etc., after he had spent an entire day in a strange place.

He was absolutely distraught, hissing and raving. My cat is usually so sweet, docile, and lets you do tests and handle him without any problem. He was out of his mind, didn't even recognize me, and attacked me. He was so scared he'd soiled himself. I asked for a room so I could be alone with him and clean him up. It took almost 10 minutes for him to recognize me. It was awful.

But the worst came later at home. He had a paste of urine and feces on his abdomen that looked like it had been there for many hours. I had to give him a full shower to get all the mess off. This leads me to believe that they didn't take him out of his cage during the 24 hours he was hospitalized and that the urine mixed with the feces...

That same day he started defecating liquid blood, probably from the stress he was under, my vet told me. He advised against a second hospitalization, even though he still wasn't eating. I thought I was going to lose him. He literally defecated blood for a whole week, and it took me four weeks to fully stabilize him with a lot of medication.

Of course, in the right hands, that was possible, but my cat left the clinic in worse condition than when I brought him in. And this is unacceptable.
I know they have other franchises, and perhaps things are better there, but in my case, it was a terrible experience. The reception staff and the animal care during the stay, in my opinion, are not the best. DO NOT take your pets there if you want peace of mind knowing they are in proper hygienic conditions and under the care of a responsible team.

I've attached a photo of the "blood" he defecated for a week to illustrate the point.

I suppose you'll respond and try to justify all these accusations. I would prefer an apology and a real attempt to do better. I'd like to see that, besides the money, you also care about the animals.

Our deepest gratitude goes to Medivet and Dr. Mar for saving our beloved dachshund, Pimienta, who was nearly paraplegic due to a herniated disc. They acted swiftly, always with clarity and communication, and most importantly, with genuine care for our dear friend! Thank you for everything!
Hello Julene Sanchez. Thank you for your review and for trusting our veterinary hospital Medivet 24-hour Veterinary Hospital Delicias. Greetings from the whole team.

They have my two-month-old Chihuahua hospitalized there, and the care is excellent. I found them online. The most important thing is that they're open 24 hours a day and have an emergency medical service. What I didn't like was that they initially told me my Chihuahua had delicate vertebrae, then later denied saying so, which is frustrating. Aside from that, I'm very happy with how they've treated my pet, and it's a fantastic place to save your best friend's life. A couple of days ago, around July 20th, I took my other Chihuahua, who is older, to the vet. She was vomiting, confused, had bloody, gelatinous discharge, and wasn't eating or drinking for hours, just vomiting there. When I arrived, I explained everything that was happening since my insurance company had sent me to the emergency room quickly for what was probably a pancreatic issue. After more than two hours and having to say a couple of times that my dog ​​was very sick, other customers kept coming in. The next time I told them I was leaving, they told me to wait a moment. The third time they said that word, I left, and of course, I'm never going back, nor do I recommend them. I was lucky with my first Chihuahua because he was a puppy. It seems that because my dog ​​is older, despite her condition, they didn't want to treat her with the priority she deserves.

The receptionist is incredibly unpleasant, the older lady; the redhead is lovely. We've had this happen with her several times before. You arrive sad to see your dog, and they make you wait as long as they deem necessary. They don't consider your personal life, only their own schedule. I've been waiting for over 50 minutes for them to bring my son, and she gets arrogant and smiles when she gives you an unexpected answer... something like, "I already notified them, and there's nothing I can do." Excuse me? 50 minutes?! That's the last thing we need right now, since we work to pay these exorbitant bills! The least they could do is try to meet the deadlines...

Our dog Lily was admitted on Monday the 13th, and they immediately ran tests and operated on her quickly.
She was hospitalized this week and was discharged yesterday.
She's doing very well considering how she was when she arrived.
Both Lily and her family are incredibly grateful for the care we received and how lovingly she was treated.
We have to go back, but our gratitude is immense; if we had been a little late, she wouldn't have made it.
Thank you so much to the entire team.

Always.

🐾❤️❤️

We will be eternally grateful; they saved our dog Lili's life. They are highly professional and treat pet owners with the utmost respect. We were kept informed of her condition and progress every step of the way. I wholeheartedly recommend this veterinary hospital to all pet lovers.
Hello Fernando Ramos Delgado. Thank you very much for your review of Medivet 24-hour Veterinary Hospital Delicias. Best regards.

In response to your reply:

I understand that the sedation and tests performed were aimed at assessing the reason for the urgent consultation. However, before the X-ray, I informed you that my cat suffers from calicivirus and chronic oral problems. Furthermore, during the consultation, I specifically asked if the oral pain could be related to his rapid breathing, and I was told yes.

That is precisely why I was surprised that, once they finally managed to sedate him after several attempts, they didn't take advantage of that moment to perform an oral examination or a basic general assessment. Not because I considered it warranted a separate consultation, but because sedating a cat that is difficult to handle is neither simple nor desirable to repeat unnecessarily.

If there was a possibility that the oral pain was contributing to the reason for the consultation, I believe it would have been reasonable to check the condition of his oral cavity, even if only to assess whether there was significant inflammation or if it was advisable to start any treatment or refer him later.

And frankly, considering the service cost €273, I believe that a basic check-up, such as opening his mouth and assessing his condition, would have been a gesture of clinical care and concern for the animal's well-being. That's the aspect of care I missed and the reason for my review.

************** I went to Medivet Delicias on a Saturday morning because my cat had been experiencing episodes of rapid breathing for a couple of days. Before going, I called Medivet Vallecas to ask about the price of the consultation and a possible chest x-ray, as cost was important to me. They recommended I go to Delicias in case it became necessary to admit the cat. Although I inquired about the prices, I would have appreciated being warned, when they referred me to another clinic, that the service would be billed as an emergency and that the cost would be considerably higher.

Upon arriving at the clinic, they presented me with a quote for an emergency consultation, x-ray, and sedation. At that moment, I agreed because my priority was getting my cat the care he needed.

The veterinarian who saw us was very kind, and the personal attention was excellent throughout. They told me to come back in about 40-60 minutes, and when I returned, they informed me that they still hadn't been able to sedate him after several attempts. At that point, I offered to go downstairs with them to help, since my cat is usually much calmer when I'm present, and on other occasions, they've been able to perform examinations and even tests without sedation, or at least make it easier to handle him while administering it. They finally managed to sedate him and take the X-ray.

Before the test, I also mentioned that my cat has calicivirus and mouth problems. That's precisely why I was surprised that, once he was sedated, they didn't take the opportunity to do a more thorough examination, check his oral cavity, or perform a general assessment. On other occasions, at different veterinary clinics, sedation has been used to perform this type of examination, avoiding the need to sedate the animal again later.

The final bill came to €273. I don't question the professionalism or the work of veterinarians, a profession I value and know requires great dedication. However, as a pet owner, I'm concerned that veterinary care costs are reaching amounts that, at least in my experience, are very difficult for many families to afford. When you pay such a high amount, you also expect the most comprehensive care possible and greater transparency from the outset.

My intention with this review is not to criticize the veterinarian who treated us, whose treatment was correct and friendly, but rather to share an experience that I believe could be improved, both in terms of communication and the care received in relation to the amount paid.

I discovered Medivet Delicias because of a respiratory emergency my pet had, and I haven't stopped going since. The care is always excellent, both professionally and personally.

Laura at reception stands out for her kindness and efficiency, making everything easy from the very first moment. Patricia and the entire team of veterinarians and assistants demonstrate great professionalism, coordination, and genuine affection for the animals, explaining everything clearly and inspiring a lot of confidence.

Special mention goes to César, the dermatologist, whose intervention was key. He dedicates the necessary time to explaining the condition and finding the solution, with amazing empathy.

A top-notch team that combines experience, dedication, and a personal touch. Highly recommended.
It's an absolute outrage to keep the animal suffering until it dies. In the end, I'd rather it spend that time with me at home; at least I'd save myself so much money and despair.

We had our dog, Toto, operated on for a hernia. They were very kind and professional throughout the entire process. Everything went very well, and the veterinary team provided excellent post-operative follow-up.

We had a very serious problem with our dachshund's herniated disc, and we couldn't have found a better center for emergency surgery!
Dr. Mar and her entire team are incredible. The service was impeccable, and above all, the care and attention they gave our dog was exceptional. They were always kind and attentive, and it's clear they truly love animals. Dr. Mar did an extraordinary job, and I would recommend this center to anyone needing veterinary care for their pet. Without a doubt, the best veterinary center I know!
A huge thank you to the whole team for your excellent work, your professionalism, and the care you showed us and our dog!
Hello Sheila. Thank you so much for your review of our 24-hour veterinary hospital. Best regards from the Medivet 24-hour Veterinary Hospital Delicias team.

I've been taking my dog ​​there for 12 years whenever I have an emergency because I don't know of any other vet, but it really depends on the vet you get. On Monday night, we had an emergency, and they barely examined him. They didn't give us a clear diagnosis and covered their bases by writing in the report that he should be reviewed by professionals from every possible area, without narrowing it down. In the morning, we had to take him to their clinic, and there they finally figured it out and treated him properly. We paid €156 for nothing.
Great service, a very pleasant surprise, I will bring my pet again.

Last Sunday I had to take my cat Bianchi to the emergency vet after she developed a very high fever. The staff were incredibly kind, professional, and helpful. She was hospitalized for three days after being diagnosed with parvovirus. The care was excellent, the attention 100/10, and my cat is now much recovered and happy. I am so grateful to the veterinarians Edrei Marrero and Mercedes Matía, and of course to all the veterinary assistants who looked after my Bianchi. ❤️🙌🏻

This weekend I had to take my German Shepherd puppy to the vet for respiratory problems. From the moment we walked in, they treated us quickly and very well. Within two hours, my dog ​​was back home with the tests completed, a diagnosis, and medication. I hope my little dog doesn't get sick again, but at least I now have a vet I can trust. I highly recommend them.

We couldn't be happier. The professionalism, care, and attention given by the Medivet team has been unparalleled. After moving from another country with our cat Maki, he started having stress-related problems upon arrival, and not knowing where else to take him, we came here. We left him there for a day, they ran tests and procedures, and we took him home much better and more at ease. After a week and a follow-up appointment, our cat has improved significantly and is back to normal.
A huge thank you in particular to Edrei Javier; we have never felt safer or more at ease, thanks to his meticulous care and how well he treated us and explained everything. An exceptional professional. 100% recommended.
Horrible service. They take out money and the forms aren't available. The emergency room is a disaster; two hours and no preparation.

Very, very bad. They made us wait two hours for X-rays in the emergency room and then told us he had edema but that we should take him somewhere else because there was no room with oxygen. I'm never going back.
They are the worst thing that ever happened to us.

My experience at this veterinary clinic was very disappointing.

I had to take my cat, Hermes, there for a weekend after being referred by my regular veterinarian. After he was admitted, I was told I would receive updates on his progress, but I didn't receive any calls and had to contact them repeatedly to try to find out how he was doing.

Due to the lack of information, I went to the clinic in person. During that visit, I had to wait a long time to be seen and didn't get any clear answers about my pet's condition. Later, I was allowed to visit him, which I appreciated.

Over the following days, I observed several situations that raised concerns about the internal organization and communication with pet owners. I also had questions about some of the treatments and charges I was being billed for, as the information provided wasn't clear enough.

Furthermore, I witnessed conversations between staff members that made me lose confidence in the clinic's management. The communication was unprofessional on several occasions, and the treatment I received from some employees fell below the standard I expected from a veterinary service.

I finally decided to transfer my cat to another clinic to continue his medical care. My negative experience stems primarily from the lack of communication, the limited information provided during his admission, and the loss of trust I felt in how the case was handled.

I'm sharing my experience so that other owners can make an informed decision.

Terrible. I took my dog ​​to the emergency vet and after making us wait almost two hours, they told us they didn't know what it could be, that with the symptoms we described they couldn't do anything, and they didn't even bother to examine him properly. I absolutely do not recommend them. They seem like fake vets; now I understand why there are so many bad reviews.
Terrible treatment, very money-grubbing, no humanity whatsoever. They returned my dog ​​injured. Don't take your pets there.
Thank you so much for your opinion, Encarni!

I want to express my deepest gratitude to the entire Medivet Delicias team, both the hospital vets and the veterinary technicians, for the care you gave my pet, for the attention and affection you showed us during these days until his recovery. You are true professionals. Thank you so much on behalf of myself, Marcos, and Milton Conchello.

And to Patricia, his regular vet, for her close and compassionate commitment to us. You do a fantastic job! Thank you, thank you, thank you.

A huge hug to everyone! Thank you, Medivet Delicias Team! 🐾🐾

My cat was admitted to the emergency vet with a creatinine level of 9. After 48 hours in the hospital, she was discharged with a level of 7. I took her home because they were only giving her food and water. When we visited her, we saw an IV line in place, but no fluids were being administered (IV fluids), and they still wanted me to keep her for another 48 hours. At my regular vet, she revived after two hours of IV fluids, which makes me even more suspicious that they didn't do anything, yet they charged me for things like "fluid therapy." I've asked them twice for a full report detailing the substances and amounts administered, and they haven't sent it, further fueling my suspicion that they're hiding something. Not to mention the lack of customer service; they say they'll call back, but they never do, and when you call, no one answers the phone. Furthermore, if you want to finance your treatment, the information is nonexistent; they don't even know the interest rates.

On Sunday, April 26th, at approximately 11 PM, I went to the emergency vet with my cat, who had lost a lot of blood. Upon arrival, they left me waiting in the waiting room for about 20 minutes while they attended to another cat whose case wasn't as serious. Then other people arrived with dogs, including a couple with a small white dog they were going to euthanize. They brought her in immediately and began the procedure in a small room next to reception, where everything could be heard, including the cries of the dog's owner and the dog herself. There was blood on the waiting room floor. I asked them to open the door for me and went to Gattos Hospital, where the treatment was completely different, showing care and respect for both my cat and me. The veterinarian, a man whose name I don't know, but given the time and date, you'll know who he is, had a passive and disinterested attitude throughout the entire situation. If you love your pet, never take them to this place. It is essential to deeply value the love and care that animals give us, and they deserve the same in their medical care. My ethical responsibility is to share this message and save other animals from ending up in this situation.
Because I can't give it less, the worst experience, very little sensitivity and humanity, budget is the most important thing for them, we would never go back
The staff are very attentive and professional, but it's also true that you pay a lot. The truth is, if you love animals, you'll do whatever it takes for them, even pay those exorbitant bills.

It was always my go-to hospital for serious cases. This time, I had to go there for something important for my dog, and they forgot to do one of the CT scans needed to confirm if there was metastasis. The cardiologist didn't know how to draw blood from my dog, leaving him riddled with holes, and the oncologist gave us a perfect lecture on how to treat cancer with chemotherapy, but she didn't seem to care that my dog ​​had been vomiting and not eating for two weeks for another reason and had a terrible mouth infection. Prices have skyrocketed, yet the service seems to have dropped. I get the feeling they're just doing their training and treating you like a credit card. I sincerely hope they invest in better professionals and truly care about animals, because it's a shame to decide not to go to the vet you thought was the best.
This place is unbeatable. They serve with empathy, joy, and heart. Elena, Laura, and Ana are delightful people. I'm very grateful to them.

Every time we've gone, they've treated us very well. With our dog, we've had to see two different specialists at different times, and they've both managed to find answers.
Sometimes it's difficult to get an appointment, and even after you do, it can take a while. I recommend patience; this happens at all vets.

This is the first time I've visited this hospital because of the good reviews, but I regret it. I took my cat to the emergency room on April 17th because she hadn't eaten or drunk anything for three days due to the pain. It turns out she had an intestinal disease, which they said was common because some cats develop it, and they said it wasn't serious. My cat seemed fine when I took her; she could walk and move perfectly, the only problem was the pain that prevented her from eating and drinking. During my visits with her, I noticed the care she received, which I think was nonexistent. They sedated her several times, which I think is an exaggeration for an animal that can't eat on its own. On one of the visits, they even bathed her, something she doesn't like, and of course, she was very upset. They didn't finish drying her, and she was shivering from the cold. I was very close to taking her home because of that. Another thing I noticed was that the cable she had attached to... Her leg, which was supposed to hold the medication, didn't have enough pull to move from one box to another. It would pull on her leg and hurt her. When we told the vet about it, she said they had forgotten. What kind of vet is she? So today I picked up my cat, the 20th, after four days. They were supposed to have sedated her again to remove the catheter, the Elizabethan collar, and the wires. Okay, they told me the anesthesia would wear off, but at 3:40 in the morning, my cat is lying there, unable to move, unable to walk, having spasms, and urinating on herself. I paid for everything they did to her. When I brought her in, she was okay, all things considered, and now they're returning her to me dying. Who knows what kind of abuse they've inflicted on my poor cat? I'm dying to file a complaint... I don't recommend this hospital at all. I know that if anything happens to my cat, I'm going to file a complaint, and they'll remember me. They don't deserve even one star. I'm so, so angry. I have to give it one star to post this, otherwise it won't let me, but they don't deserve even one star.
Thank you so much for your feedback!
Excellent care for pets. The veterinary professionals were very ethical and kind in their treatment of the animals and pets. The equipment and procedures are very comprehensive.

I took my dog ​​Blimky to the emergency vet on the advice of my regular veterinarian, and I have to say that Cristina, the surgeon, performed a rather complicated cholecystectomy and saved her life. Both she and the rest of the team were attentive and empathetic, and they treated Blimky very well during her stay and afterward at the follow-up appointments. Thank you so much for everything.

Hello Juan Victorio Serrano Patiño. We don't have enough information to identify your visit. If you'd like to clarify, our veterinary hospital, Medivet 24-hour Veterinary Hospital Delicias, can review it once you provide us with the necessary information.

Scammers! They run tons of tests, want to keep him hospitalized, and the diagnosis they give you is completely wrong. I had to take my dog ​​somewhere else. I went to the emergency room, and what I saw was that they just want to charge you for every possible test, only to end up giving him painkillers and fever reducers without addressing the infection because, according to Dr. Daniel, he didn't have one. I had taken my dog ​​there before for the emergency room, and all the doctors there agreed with his trusted vet, but now with this doctor, the service and diagnosis are terrible. It seems like he gets incentives to do more tests, but he can't even get the diagnosis right! It's awful. I asked for a stomach protector for my dog, and he ignored me. But he's quick to charge for X-rays and wants to do ultrasounds. I think a lot of people profit from the love we have for our pets; that doctor is more of a salesman than a veterinarian.
The service was excellent and fast. My dog ​​is elderly and has a heart condition, so anything could go wrong. Paloma was a delight.

Today we went to Medivet Delicias to get our furry friend's teeth cleaned. The reception staff were incredibly friendly and welcoming.
The professionals at the clinic attended to us immediately, even though we arrived early.
Hello Elena Patier. Thank you so much for your feedback on our 24-hour veterinary services and emergency care. Best regards from the entire Medivet 24-hour Veterinary Hospital Delicias team.
Excellent service. Luis and María del Mar...
They almost killed our dog! And the price they charged was an absolute rip-off. I will never go back and I will never recommend it to anyone.

I have nothing but words of gratitude for the entire team, thanks to Dr. Cristina Sotuela, veterinarian Paloma, Iván and his colleague (please excuse me for not knowing his name), and everyone on the team who saved my dog. I will be eternally grateful to Medivet Delicias. I went there as an emergency after a critical situation, and today I am able to write this and continue with my pet, thanks to you all. Sara and Dama.
Excellent service, very helpful and friendly! I'm leaving feeling very reassured ☺️
Excellent service and good professionals
Excellent service.

Thank you from the bottom of my heart for the help provided during my dog's stay by all the staff at MEDIVET. A group of trustworthy professionals who showed care and empathy from the very first moment. When we face difficult times with our animals, it's invaluable to have the support of such highly skilled and trustworthy specialists. Thank you to Patricia and her entire team.

I have nothing but praise for this clinic. My dog ​​was admitted on Friday, referred by her vet, and has been very well cared for by both Patricia, who is wonderful, and Iván. I was able to visit her every day she was admitted, and they called me in the morning to give me a daily update. They discharged her when Patricia saw that I could take her home—not before, not after—because, as she says, there's no place like home. They gave me her report, and everything was very well explained, including the appropriate medication regimen. It's great that they have their own pharmacy across the street, so you can take the medication home without having to search for a pharmacy that stocks it, which can sometimes be a real ordeal. I've read comments from people who are upset about the waiting time, but since it's an emergency center, there's a triage system in place. If your pet were very ill, you'd want others to let you be seen first, and that's exactly what happens here. All I know is that if I had to choose an emergency center, I would choose them again. Thank you, Patricia and Iván! Signed, Lúa

Yes. It can happen.
Not always, but it's a known risk, especially in geriatric animals and those with metastasis.

1️⃣ Surgical Stress and the Immune System
Surgery causes:
intense stress
systemic inflammation
release of cortisol (the stress hormone)
👉 All of this temporarily suppresses the immune system.

In a young, healthy animal, the body recovers.

In a 14-year-old dog with metastatic cancer, this drop in defenses can be critical.

2️⃣ The Cancer Was Already There, But…
It’s important to be precise:
❌ Surgery doesn’t create cancer
✅ But it can deprive the body of what little ability it had to contain it
The cancer cells:

were already in the lung
were “controlled” in a precarious balance
After surgery:
the body goes into survival mode
prioritizes healing
stops “monitoring” the cancer
👉 This can lead to faster and more visible progression.

3️⃣ Anesthesia and Age
In very old dogs:
anesthesia can affect the lungs, liver, and kidneys;
recovery is slow or incomplete.
If there was already lung metastasis:
any respiratory deterioration
or extreme fatigue
can cause very rapid decline.

We are so grateful to the entire team for all their efforts in saving our daughter. Any other facility, seeing that she was elderly, wouldn't have done half as much. We appreciate the treatment we received at all times and how well cared for she was; she was always attended to and monitored, and everyone there knew her after just five days in the hospital. We saw firsthand where she was and how all the staff spoke to her and cared for her as if she were their own child. She has passed away, and we are, of course, devastated, but our hearts are full knowing that everything possible was done and she passed away peacefully. Thank you all so much.

I don't even know how to explain it; we're devastated by the loss of our kitten. Something happened to her on Sunday; we thought she fell from a low place, and she hurt herself badly. She was meowing and hissing in pain. We called the clinic because ours was closed and explained the situation. They told us to keep an eye on her and that if her paw didn't swell, she didn't develop a fever, or she stopped eating, they recommended waiting until the next day, as it would likely improve.

In the afternoon, we called again because she was still the same; she couldn't move at all because of the pain. They told us the same thing: it didn't seem life-threatening and it was best to leave her alone.
The next day, we went to her vet since he's close to home, and the x-rays didn't show any fractures... from then on, everything went wrong, and she passed away within hours without us knowing what really happened to her.
I suppose their advice was well-intentioned, but it was definitely a matter of life or death. We can't know for sure, but perhaps those extra hours could have saved her life, and she'd be with us now. She was fine, with perfect blood work a month ago... the loss is compounded by not knowing what happened to her and the feeling of not having done enough for her.
Years ago, our rabbit was admitted there; it was a tough experience, but they took wonderful care of him and saved his life. That's why we trusted them and followed their advice—they're the professionals. But we should have taken our cat there ourselves, without asking any questions.
Please be very careful with recommendations; these are our lives, our loved ones, and it's always hard to lose them, especially in this way.

I didn't want to leave a bad review, but whenever I tell people about it, some tell me to do it, and others already knew this clinic had a bad reputation. Seeing and reading the negative reviews, I felt a connection.

My dog ​​had a very strong reaction to a bite on his snout and also severe diarrhea. I took him in on a Sunday at midday, and they completely dismissed it. They gave him an antihistamine, and I went home without his Elizabethan collar or anything. He improved a little until the evening, when I saw he was worse than when I'd gone at midday. I called that night and told them he was worse and that I wanted to bring him in, but if possible, I asked them not to charge me more than for the Elizabethan collar and to take a look at him. The response was: if you come in, we're going to charge you the same as at midday, as if it were a new appointment (€120!!). After arguing with both the vet and the receptionist who's sometimes at reception, I decided to go back at 4 a.m. They were kind enough to charge me €80, and only because I told them it was their negligence. The receptionist showed absolutely no empathy towards me or the animal. And I should mention that we waited a full half hour for the vet to come up, so it's no wonder people get angry or leave with their pet dead. I thought it was monstrous. Don't go there if it's very serious or urgent.

Excellent service at this clinic. Although we had to wait a bit because it was a nighttime emergency, our dog is already feeling better, and the vet answered all our questions calmly and very kindly. Our experience was positive.

My friend recommended this veterinary hospital for my cat's surgery, and the staff were exceptional in treating both my pet and me. He was hospitalized for four days, and they called me every day to update me on his condition and the treatments he was receiving. I highly recommend it.

I took my dog ​​Lola to this clinic for an emergency after she started vomiting and I suspected an obstruction. Over the phone, they warned me it was most likely just indigestion from giving her treats, but I decided to come in to be sure. They took an X-ray which clearly showed two dehydrated cow tails obstructing her intestine. At the pet store where I bought them, they told me they were digestive aids; they weren't very big, and I thought they were the closest thing to nerves, so I never imagined they could cause such a serious problem.

Even so, the vet downplayed the situation: she told me I could leave her there just to monitor the vomiting and diarrhea, or take her home and come back in the morning for an ultrasound. I asked if she could die that night, and she replied no, that she had seen dogs with nails in their intestines and they had survived on their own, and that I should stay calm.

With this information, I took her home, but seeing that she was still very restless, I called another clinic. They told me that's not how it's done, that the ultrasound had to be done immediately to check for an intestinal perforation or even peritonitis, something that can't be detected with a simple X-ray. They also explained that she needed blood work and had to be hospitalized because she was very dehydrated, needed IV fluids, and pain medication. Nothing like what they told me at this clinic.

Furthermore, I had to deal with an assistant who constantly made judgmental faces at me for giving her treats, and who treated me terribly on the phone, in a curt and very unpleasant manner, saying that according to the vet, she should have stayed, which was also false and pointless, because this clinic wasn't going to do any of the things the second clinic did.

Finally, at the second clinic, upon seeing the same X-rays, they clearly saw that the intestine was inflamed due to the obstruction, something the first clinic hadn't even mentioned. My dog ​​was already very weak and, obviously, had to be admitted. She needs emergency surgery in a few hours because the obstruction is severe and dangerous.

I'm sharing this because, although I know there can be different veterinary opinions, here a critical situation that endangered my dog's life was downplayed. They didn't act with the necessary urgency, the risks weren't properly explained, and the treatment was unacceptable. I hope my experience helps prevent others from going through the same thing.
Excellent hospital, thank you for taking such professional and kind care of my furry friend.

We called to schedule an emergency appointment, and we arrived within 20 minutes. After registering our pet at reception and being told we'd be seen shortly, we waited almost two hours (45 minutes longer than the previous animal ahead of us). The entire staff disappeared, and the place began to smell of food. When we tried to leave, the door was locked. We called the clinic (phone was disconnected), then tried voicemail, and after 10 minutes, a woman appeared to tell us they were attending to the patients in the basement… all the staff? Four people attending to the animals in the basement and no one at reception. As we were leaving, the veterinarian, Iván, called us to scold us for not letting him know we were waiting (apparently, there's no communication among his staff to indicate they have patients waiting). A very bad experience at the emergency clinic.
I left delighted. They were very attentive and professional. ☺️ 🐈 …
The service and attention were excellent. They treat pets with love and professionalism; you can tell they care about them ❤️. And they have great facilities!
Many thanks to the entire Medivet Delicias team for your friendly service!

We're sorry your experience wasn't the best. As a 24-hour emergency veterinary hospital, we want to know how we can improve. If you'd like to share more about your experience, please write to us at comunicacion@medivetgroup.es.
Terrible experience, I would never recommend this veterinarian.
We would like to better understand your experience at our 24-hour emergency veterinary hospital. If you can share more details, please contact us at comunicacion@medivetgroup.es.

I had a very painful experience at this veterinary clinic. I took my cat in for an operation that I was told was low-risk. Unfortunately, my cat passed away during the procedure. Beyond the loss itself, what affected me most was the lack of transparency from the staff. I didn't feel they gave me enough explanations about what happened, nor did they show the sensitivity one expects in such a situation.

I understand that there are always risks involved in veterinary medicine, but I believe there was a significant lack of communication. It's important that other people are aware of these kinds of situations so they can make informed decisions about where to entrust the care of their pets.

My experience at this clinic wasn't very good. My cat died during surgery to remove stones that were obstructing his digestive system. It was a seemingly simple operation, but sadly, my cat passed away.
From what I was told, the cat didn't wake up from the anesthesia. I've requested the reports (which they haven't sent me yet) so I can understand the reasons and compare them with specialists. Later, I read very bad reviews of this clinic. If I had read them beforehand, I probably wouldn't have had him operated on here. 😢

We arrived at the emergency vet at 4 a.m. with a very weak dog who wasn't responding to any stimuli. The waiting room was completely empty, and a receptionist with no apparent knowledge greeted us coldly and told us to wait. After a long wait without hearing from anyone, we asked several times for someone to see us, but neither the receptionist nor the veterinarian responded. We decided to go to another veterinary hospital due to the lack of compassion at that place. As we were leaving, the "veterinarian" magically appeared, saying, "See you later," followed by some very inappropriate remarks. It's clear that this is a business, and they care little to nothing about the animals' health.

It's worth mentioning that we had been taking our pet to them for over two years; he was like family. It doesn't matter how much money you've spent or how many times they've seen you cry for your furry friends; their only goal is to make money.

If you care even a little about your animals and value kind, humane treatment, please don't go to that hospital. They are heartless and shameless.

I hope they get what they deserve.

A personal piece of advice for the people who work at that center: "You have to treat people with tact, respect, courtesy, and a lot of empathy, especially when they are treating you this way, and even more so in the circumstances that lead you to these places." Our dog died that same night, and the treatment was absolutely appalling. I don't know the name of the veterinarian who saw us early Friday morning, the 18th, but I hope you are aware of the place where you work and stop to think that it's not just a job; you are dealing with people who have feelings (even if you don't know what that means), and when you go to a veterinary hospital at 4 a.m., it's not by choice.
We took our dog to the emergency vet and the service was excellent. They were quick and very attentive. 100% recommended.

My dog ​​had botched Legg-Calvé-Perthes surgery here, and although they responded with a copy-and-paste of my initial post, they never took responsibility. I'm furious to see my dog ​​constantly in pain because they cut his femur incorrectly, leaving a splinter that rubs against his hip socket. Small dogs usually recover very well from this surgery. They've ruined mine.
Delighted with the service I received and grateful for the work of Iván Cepeda and Liliana, who were on duty the night I had to take my Gara in. Thank you so much.
We love receiving reviews like yours. As a 24-hour emergency hospital, we're always available for you and your pet.

February 26, 2026 Update: I resent the email, they replied asking me to explain the situation, I explained everything, and I haven't heard from them since.
It's an investment fund. They have a monthly target to reach, and they achieve it by charging us from every angle.

January 31, 2025 Update: They're not replying to emails.

November 11, 2024 They have absolutely no scruples. I was there 10 minutes ago; they tried to resuscitate my kitten, but it wasn't possible, and they charged me 160 euros for 15 minutes of resuscitation. On top of that, they charged 180 euros for cremation. They take advantage of the love we have for our pets. (Furthermore, the assistant asked the veterinarian, "We're only charging for the cremation, right?" And the other one, without any shame, replied: "No, no, the resuscitation too.")

It's been over three months since my Dachshund had surgery at this clinic! I couldn't be more grateful for the care and the results! Pancho came out looking like nothing had been done to him. His recovery was incredibly fast.
Excellent service, outstanding professionals, very kind, and very empathetic and understanding. Thank you very much.

My cat Laia had surgery there for pyometra, two mastectomies performed by Lucia, a surgeon who retired last summer. She always saved and cured her. Now, with the cancer more advanced, I spent almost 500 euros on tests that only served to tell me that she had to be put down. We thought she was doing relatively well, so we brought her home. She ate, drank, even played; we were able to enjoy her and she enjoyed us in these last few weeks. I was prescribed Stilsona. When the first bottle ran out, we called several times throughout the day and received no answer. Seeing that we were desperate because night was approaching and it was time for her to take it, we insisted, but they weren't at all pleasant. They prescribed it, and when my husband, who went there, asked how long the Stilsona should be used, the vet there rudely told him to make an appointment next time to see the tumor. They never showed any concern or called to ask about Laia. We felt abandoned, especially since I've spent over 6,000 euros at this clinic on various surgeries, treatments, and tests.
On Monday at 3:30 in the morning, my cat had a crisis. We already knew it was the end, and she, sweet as always, lay down, wagged her tail, and looked at us as if to say, "I can't go on." That day she played, she was happy, she ate...
When we arrived, the girl there was very cold, unfriendly, and rude. She was the one who called the vet, who came up and told us they were going to put her to sleep. I was always told to be with her when they put her to sleep, calm and seeing each other before the euthanasia injection, but it wasn't like that. They shaved her paw, and with her last bit of strength, she meowed. They weren't gentle at all. They couldn't get the IV in, and she screamed. She bled quite a bit, and they told us they were taking her downstairs to put the IV in. My youngest daughter left, and I left because of her screaming. My older daughter and my husband stayed inside, waiting, and when they finally brought her up, they told us... "Quick, she's going!" While we were on the benches, and she was in the first room on the right, her mouth was already open, wet with urine, and she was lifeless.

They charged me almost 500 euros for individual cremation, euthanasia, and writing up the information. They said they'd call me the next day because we wanted some jewelry to carry her ashes, and today is Thursday, and as always during these 12 years, not a single call. I can't stop crying because I don't know what they did to my cat down there. She didn't die seeing us or with us. I don't know what they did to her or what they put her in to cause such a quick and painful death.

The vet was like a statue. I just cried and asked her questions, terrified... Did she suffer? Will you clean her up? What will you do with her? Are you sure she's dead? They told me beforehand that they might check her muscles, that they would listen to her heartbeat. They don't tell you anything afterward! They just sat down and started writing the bill. It was all very cold, and all they wanted was for us to pay and leave, leaving my life companion there on a cold table.

I get the feeling they just wanted us to leave as soon as possible.
I have another 9-month-old adopted kitten whom I thought about taking there, but no way! Lucía, who was a wonderful surgeon, is no longer there. Now the company has changed, and it's awful.
By the way, the cremation place is on the road to the reservoirs, very far away. There are closer places, which I only found out about later. It's a real shame, especially considering all the money we spent there. They have new staff every time you go, and they're not at all affectionate, even though they talk to you as if they were. We really miss Lucía, who spoke to you and told you things directly.

On February 10th, I was with a little dog, Pequi, who had already been to other vets and wasn't improving, so I decided to take her to the hospital.
On Saturday, at another vet, she had an ultrasound and blood test which showed an imbalance in her sodium and potassium levels, suggesting that she might have Addison's disease. My dog ​​arrived at the vet at eight in the morning, but they didn't see us until 10:00 because there was a shift change. When they finally saw us, I explained everything to the vet, telling her about the decompensation. This decompensation, if it's Addison's disease, only appears during an Addisonian crisis. That said, what's inexplicable is that I told them this at ten in the morning, and then, after I had requested and reviewed the tests done at the other clinic, they decided to repeat the tests at three in the afternoon and then do the cortisol test. Obviously, the dog couldn't endure that much time and died of cardiorespiratory arrest because in a crisis you have to act quickly, and because they took so long to attend to her, my daughter didn't make it in time. Besides, if they had seen her earlier, they would have noticed that her pulse was low.

My advice is that if you're going to a hospital, go to the Reina Cristina Veterinary Emergency Clinic. It's not a clinic and a hospital; it's just a hospital, meaning they don't offer consultations. Our dogs are cared for 24 hours a day, and these kinds of things don't happen there. I recently had to take another dog to the Reina Cristina Veterinary Emergency Clinic, and they had already seen him before I even got home.

Obviously, this won't bring my dog ​​back, but it will prevent you from taking other dogs there and having them wait five hours without being seen.

If you truly love your pet, don't come here. All they care about is making money. To them, we're just walking ATMs. Not to mention that my cat came in relatively well, but within two days she was in terrible condition and died a few days later. The receptionist had zero empathy. We took our other cat to a different hospital further away, even though it's right next to our house.
The worst part is that a year after she died, they sent me a text message wishing me a happy birthday.
Thank you for trusting us! We will continue working diligently to always offer you the best in 24-hour veterinary care.

March 1, 2025 I'm still waiting for a reply to my email.

December 28, 2024 I was very happy with them until now, but since the oncologist left, the service has been appalling. She only holds consultations once a week, they tell you to send an email with any questions and she'll answer them, and I've been waiting for her to answer my questions since December 23rd. I've already had to put my cat to sleep without her replying. Thanks for everything!

I'm so happy with the care my kitten received. The vet (I don't remember her name) was incredibly nice and knew how to handle my cat (which is difficult because he gets very nervous). He even seemed comfortable! Thank you for treating and caring for him.

I am so grateful to Mar and the entire team for all the help they have given us. Cares, my dog, spent a very sick year with meningitis, and thanks to their care and attention, he has made a wonderful recovery. They have always been attentive, caring, and very professional.

Thank you for everything!
Excellent veterinary hospital with a team that truly cares about the health and well-being of pets. Personalized attention, spotless facilities, and top-notch professionals. Highly recommended!

My review is about the shop, as they aren't our usual vets. Laura is a lovely person, professional and very kind; she provides excellent service and helps you find what you need. She also always gives me great advice on the best care for my pets, and we're delighted.

I took my dog ​​in for a fractured femur and patella, and the surgery was quick. It's a franchise company; ultimately, they've set up a business that takes advantage of people's lack of knowledge and the need to arrive scared with their pets. Everyone there is an apprentice, and then the orthopedic surgeon only comes once or twice a week. The prices are exorbitant, and they offer payment options with Frakmenta, but you end up with the debt. They take advantage of you at that moment; they don't explain anything. Now I'm taking my pet back for a check-up, and they tell me that he needs another surgery. The dog looks terrible; his leg is dangling, and the bone looks badly healed. They're butchers with animals, and the veterinary association should investigate whether they're truly authorized as a veterinary medical center and whether the staff is qualified.

I've read more than 17 negative reviews, and they all agree on the same thing: the worst procedures. We're still fighting this battle, trying to figure out how our dog will recover and continuing to look for an orthopedic surgeon who can help us. If you're going to take your dog there, run!

They leave their boxes abandoned on the street, littering it (there are two containers 40 meters apart), and many times the boxes end up fallen onto the road, vandalized, or scattered around by the local homeless. They've been asked to move the cardboard boxes to the container or put them out at a different time so they aren't on the sidewalk from 9 a.m. and sometimes all night long. Their response was: "Who do you think you are?"

The worst pet clinic and hospital I've ever seen. The treatment from the veterinarians was awful; if you ask what's wrong with the dog or if it's eaten, the answer is, "I don't know, I didn't bring it in." I've never encountered such staff (because you can't call them professionals) in my life. We took my dog ​​in very sick, they did blood work which showed her white blood cell count was extremely high, and none of the employees thought to give her antibiotics. They just wanted to keep running tests even though my dog ​​had a very large swelling of her gallbladder and stump from pyometra, which they didn't see in the supposed ultrasound they performed. I even doubt they did the ultrasound because when I decided to take my dog ​​out of there, my trusted clinic couldn't believe their ultrasound results; they even told me it corresponded to another dog.
The result? She was hospitalized for another 6 days at the Reina Cristina Veterinary Hospital (100% recommended and very close to this place), and sadly, my dog ​​had to leave us.

They're liars who assured me they spoke with my vet daily, but in the four days she was there, there wasn't a single call… they only called when I requested her discharge and said I was going back to my own vet… unbelievable…

Luna didn't have an insulinoma; it was ruled out with a simple blood test. You wanted to bill me for a special test plus a CT scan… Money is all you care about, the animal certainly doesn't.

Not to mention that you called me saying my dog ​​had a tumor, when I decided to take Luna home because nothing they were doing to her seemed right. That shameless vet told me it was a lie (THANK GOODNESS I HAVE ALL THE CALLS AND CLINIC TIME RECORDED BECAUSE SOMETHING TOLD ME THEY WEREN'T TRUSTWORTHY). Ma'am, the only liar here is YOU and the clinic where you work. Just lies to squeeze money out of people who go there only wanting their pet to be saved…

On top of everything, you have to put up with being called a liar; what you're doing is unforgivable.

If you need to go to a real hospital in an emergency, choose Reina Cristina Hospital. They offer daily calls twice a day, and you can see your loved one WHENEVER YOU WANT, without an appointment. They're compassionate and caring. Just read the reviews of both places… THERE'S NO COMPARISON.

It was my first time at this clinic, and honestly, I hope I never have to go back. First, when I called, the person who answered told me that although they were fully booked, they could see me when they had an opening (it was 6:30 pm on a Friday). Imagine my surprise when, upon hearing the prices, they charged me an emergency fee (90 euros for a consultation, even though it was normal business hours). I agreed because I was worried about my dog. Then, after performing an ultrasound, they only gave me a report and refused to provide the images from the test I had paid for. After insisting that they had to provide them, they told me they would send them on Monday. On Monday, I called several times, and it was all just excuses... surprise, Monday ended, and no one sent me anything. I must say that after complaining through Medivet's email, I finally got them to send me the images, but seriously... what kind of professionalism is that where you have to harass and practically threaten them to get tests you've paid for?

Zero seriousness and 10 for ripping people off...

*COMPLAINT TO MEDIVET: ONLY ONE VETERINARIAN ON EMERGENCY DUTY!*

Good afternoon, I'm writing to congratulate veterinarian Silvia, who treated my dog ​​early this morning. She explained everything clearly and in detail. I was scared at first, but I left feeling much calmer thanks to her instructions. 👩🏻‍⚕️ I also want to congratulate the receptionist or veterinary assistant (please excuse me if I'm mistaken about the job title) for her kindness at all times. HOWEVER, I want to file a COMPLAINT because I think it's excessive workload to have ONLY ONE veterinarian on EMERGENCY duty. I say this because today a man also came in with his sick kitten and started yelling at the veterinarian about the lack of staff and because he wanted almost immediate attention. I understand this gentleman's position, but I find it completely unfair that he's lashing out at a veterinarian who might not even own the clinic, and on top of that, there was only one veterinarian for all the patients who came in. I think it's serious that MEDIVET doesn't have at least two veterinarians on duty in the emergency room. Anyone who's agitated or nervous could come in and do something to those workers; there's no security because it's just two women working alone. I think it's very wrong, and I hope you'll take my review into account. I'm not complaining about her; on the contrary, I want to congratulate them for putting up with so much, but I think it's very wrong that MEDIVET doesn't have more staff in the emergency room. That's the only problem I have so far. I hope this good service I'm experiencing doesn't disappoint me.

I'm only giving stars because of her and the assistant on that shift that day; otherwise, I wouldn't give any.

It's wonderful to go to a veterinary clinic like this. It was recommended to me when my dog ​​was very sick, and after visiting several, it was the best thing that happened to me. The assistants and secretaries are lovely, professional, and very patient, but above all, it was the veterinarian, Dr. Mar, who was phenomenal. She's an indisputable professional, always looking after my dog ​​as if he were her own, and she saved him. I will be eternally grateful to her. Thank you so much, Mar. I recommend this clinic, as I always do. Don't hesitate!

Thank you so much to the whole team for being so professional, such wonderful people, and for taking such loving and respectful care of our little ones. I've been lucky enough to meet Mar, a fantastic professional who is always willing to help and dedicates the necessary time to each patient with so much love, care, and empathy. Thank you from the bottom of my heart for treating and caring for my daughters so well. 🐶
If you care about your pet, I recommend you go somewhere else. We were treated badly, and our pet was treated even worse.
It was perfect, I left very happy, they were very attentive and always called to check on the dog 10/10 times

I am so grateful to the whole team, and Lizzie, my kitten, is very happy now. I took her in sick because she was vomiting... She'd been there for about 14 hours... I felt something wasn't right. At first, it didn't seem serious, but they advised an ultrasound in case she had swallowed a thread... and thank goodness I listened to them. It was indeed a thread that had gotten tangled in her intestine. The surgeon had to open her up in four places to remove the thread without cutting part of her intestine. It was a very important operation, and thank God she recovered very well.

I honestly recommend the clinic. I had to ask my family for financial help, but my kitten survived. I only have one piece of advice for anyone who adopts a cat... You have to consider what an operation might entail, and if you don't have the means, as can happen to older people like me who are given a kitten... It's best to think twice... Because then it's too late.

Thank you so much and sorry for the length of the text. Thank you 😍😻😻
I was there because of a death, the staff were incredibly empathetic and kind, thank you so much for everything.

I wanted to thank the Medivet 24 Horas Delicias hospital. The service was wonderful. Dr. Mar, the veterinarian, did a magnificent job; she's a true professional, and her approach was very kind and caring. A month ago, I took my dog ​​in for emergency treatment because she had become paralyzed due to a severe herniated disc. Dr. Mar operated on her, and she's doing very well now, thanks to God and Dr. Mar's excellent work. Thank you so much! 😘

I had to delete my previous review to write a new one. I wanted to thank this hospital for saving my dog's life for the second time, Mar for the first time, the surgeons, and Ana, the morning receptionist, for putting up with my calls and running my errands. We live very far away, but as soon as the dog has something "serious," I don't hesitate to take him there. Thank you again.

I took my dog ​​to the emergency vet, and they misdiagnosed him. They charged me for medication he didn't need, in addition to the exorbitant bill of €283. I called to speak with them, they said they would call me back, but they never did.
I DO NOT RECOMMEND THEM AT ALL.

They were completely unprofessional. I called with an important question because I have this insurance, and the receptionist said she would check with the veterinarian and get back to me right away, but she never did. Honestly, you pay for insurance to have better coverage and peace of mind, not to be ignored.

24-hour weekend emergency experience. They are overwhelmed. There are very few staff members, although the service is good, but there isn't even anyone at reception to open the street door for you, either to enter or leave. You're locked in the waiting room, which is dangerous in case of a fire. There's no emergency ultrasound machine, which I consider essential. Without enough staff, it's impossible to treat pets well, but the prices are very reasonable.
ADDENDUM: The service was excellent; I have no complaints about that. I will return if needed, but it could be improved by having someone permanently at reception and by allowing the door to be opened from inside. Thank you very much.

My congratulations to all the staff; I'm truly delighted. I've been treating my dogs Luna and Canela here for five years, and I'm very satisfied with the excellent care they receive. Five months ago, Canela arrived in very bad shape, and I had surgery. Thanks to the help of all the staff, especially the neurosurgeon, Mar, who had a cervical hernia, she recovered in a week. At 12 years old, I'm so grateful. Thank you so much!

My dog ​​had a simple sprain, and they wanted to perform an arthrodesis (irreversible surgery with a plate that limits mobility); they were also pressuring us to pay for the plate before we even had the CT scan results. Fortunately, we got a second opinion, and no surgery was necessary. I would never recommend this clinic.

The service was terrible. They said we'd get the CT scan results in one or two days, but it's been over five and nothing. They say my dog ​​has some torn ligaments, and the surgeon wants us to pay for the operation now, but without even knowing the CT scan results. I feel like I'm being taken for a ride. They're playing with my dog's health, and they won't give me the results...

I'M NOT GOING BACK
After two years of my dog ​​receiving prescribed treatment at this clinic, they REFUSED to give me a solution in a VITAL EMERGENCY. They only want to make money.
